evidence.note: Dedup by OPERATION on the schedule.order change: (1) DEFAULT_ORDER single-sourced in ddflow/adapters/schedule_keys.py so config_sections (imports adapters only) and core.schedule share it without importing each other — deduplicating the core->config_sections broken contract that was B0db4e156e8 root cause; (2) _order_problem/_pin_problem reuse _keys_problem (2nd occurrence, shared); (3) merge_pin is the single tighten-only layered-list merge, reused for ORDER_PIN inside _core._merge_layer. DEFAULT_ORDER (static config default) vs _filters.ORDER (mutable runtime register_key list) are two distinct roles. Record-dedupe: bug B0db4e156e8 / fix-B0db4e156e8 / SCHED-order-knob relationship already documented in SCHED-order-knob body ("do that fix here or close it with this regression test"); no unsettled dup. Recorded (buglane39).

chunk_findings.detail: The pinned default order is `("recover_first", "bugs_first", "unphased_first", "priority", "id")`, but the accepted decision this change is meant to fix says the scheduler order is `bugs_first, priority ascending, id`. With the default configuration and no user override, the effective order therefore begins with `recover_first`, not `bugs_first`; a task selected by the recovery key can be ordered ahead of a bug task, so the code still disagrees with the accepted priority semantics. The new `[schedule].order` knob makes the wrong default configurable, but does not make the default itself match the accepted decision.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/schedule_keys.py:12

chunk_findings.detail: The new `order` knob documents the default order as `[recover_first, bugs_first, unphased_first, priority, id]`, while the adjacent `bugs_first` knob still says bug fixes are offered before features and that a standing bug is fixed before more features are built. With the default configuration, if the ready set contains an interrupted feature and an open bug, the documented order ranks the interrupted feature first because `recover_first` precedes `bugs_first`; that contradicts the bug-first guarantee and the accepted decision cited in the intent. The same new text also says `bugs_first = false` only makes the `bugs_first` key neutral, whereas the existing `bugs_first` documentation says `false` orders by priority alone; with the new default order, `false` would still leave `recover_first` and `unphased_first` ahead of priority.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/schedule.py:290

chunk_findings.detail: The new `order` row states that asking an agent to “offer the critical path first” means setting `schedule.order` to `["critical_path","priority","id"]`, but the newly added `order_pin` row says pinned keys go ahead of `order`. In a documented configuration where a company/lower layer sets `order_pin = ["bugs_first"]` (the example the upgrade note says a company floor keeps pinned), following the guide and setting `schedule.order = ["critical_path","priority","id"]` yields an effective order that begins with `bugs_first`, not `critical_path`. The guide’s instruction therefore does not accomplish the stated goal in the presence of pins and is wrong/incomplete.
chunk_findings.title: docs/guide/parallelism.md:312

chunk_findings.detail: `_order_problem` only enforces the `id` tie-break when `id` is already present: `if last_id and "id" in v and v[-1] != "id"`. A user can set `[schedule].order = ["priority"]` and validation returns `""`, so the configuration is accepted even though the effective order contains no `id` key; `_pin_problem` separately forbids putting `id` in `order_pin`. That violates the file’s own invariant that `id` is the deterministic tie-break and must come last: tasks with equal priority are then ordered by whatever incidental ready-set order the scheduler happens to see, making selection nondeterministic.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/schedule.py:_order_problem

data.probe: effective_order returns [*names, 'id'] unconditionally (_filters.py:89-90), so id is deterministically appended LAST whether or not the user wrote it: order=['priority'] -> base=['priority'], names=['priority'], return ['priority','id']. 'id omitted -> appended' is the documented contract (order knob doc: 'omitted, it is appended; anywhere else, refused'), so accepting ['priority'] is correct, not a nondeterminism.
